cvs: 'Green Cascade' – weeping, deeply cut green leaves · 'Cascade Gold' – compact weeping yellow-orange · 'Osakazuki' – upright, famous crimson autumn colour
foliage: deciduous; five- to seven-lobed leaves, coppery red in spring, green in summer, red and orange in autumn
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and Northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C, though young spring growth can be damaged by late frosts.
prune: Little needed. Remove dead, damaged or crossing shoots only when fully dormant (Nov-Jan), because cuts bleed if made in spring.
resilience: Fully hardy once established but leaves brown in drying wind, strong afternoon sun or drought. Pests: aphids; verticillium wilt and coral spot can occur.
soilWarning: Leaves scorch in cold wind and hot sun
uncertain: identity: the Forge name was 'Acer palmatum cascade'; RHS 366747 'Cascade' is an arching, non-dissected tree to about 3 m, which matches Oscar's photo; the draft assumed a weeping dissected form and was rewritten
seed-raised: nursery notes and a UBC forum say plants sold as 'Cascade' are often seed-grown and may vary
size: Coolings 3 × 2.5 m at 20 years; RHS 2.5–4 m
hardiness: no cultivar-specific rating found; H6 as for Acer palmatum and every Acer palmatum card in the deck
peak: sold on autumn colour (Oct-Nov); coppery spring leaves named in visual
toxicity: no hazard recorded for A. palmatum; sycamore and box elder, not this species, poison horses
uses: Patio containers · Japanese-style gardens · small gardens · sheltered borders · beside water features
visual: Fiery red and orange autumn colour on arching branches · coppery-red spring leaves, red twigs
water: Water through dry spells, especially in pots and in its first two summers; keep evenly moist but never waterlogged.
